extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, court-martial recorders, military commanders, and reviewing officers involved in military justice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing, formatting, and reviewing the official record of court-martial proceedings and for action by the reviewing authority. Covers what must appear in the record, how irregularities and amendments are handled, and limits on reviewing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all proceedings (even irregular)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the better practice that all the proceedings — even those that are irregular — which transpire in connection with a trial or at a revision should be set out in the record for the information of the reviewing authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not encumber the record with documents excluded by the court, but specify the character of such writings and the grounds on which they were excluded (R. 26, 251; R. 49, 614).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening order prefixed and complete
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the convening order should properly be prefixed to the proceedings as constituting the initial authority for the existence and action of the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order should be complete and show by heading and subscription that it proceeded from a commanding officer competent to order the court. Where several cases are tried by the same court, a separate copy of the order should be incorporated in the record in each case (R. 32, 130; R. 4, 607). Subsequent orders modifying composition should follow or be elsewhere incorporated; note when new members take their seats (R. 13, 384; R. 29, 604).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show authority for each member
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of proceedings of a general court-martial should show the authority under which each member of the court acts as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony from inferior courts not required written
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony taken before inferior courts-martial need not be reduced to writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as a specific exception to the general requirement to set forth testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show organization and quorum
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should show that the court met and organized pursuant to the order or orders constituting it, including that at least a quorum (five officers for a general court-martial) assembled at the time and place indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the members present by name, rank, etc., at first assembling; the record should show at least five members present and acting at every day's session throughout the trial (R. 3, 413; R. 6, 384). Avoid referring to a previous trial's record to identify members; for subsequent sessions a form like 'Present, all the members of the court and the judge advocate' is acceptable (P. 42, 395).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show accused's presence at organization and material stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should show the presence of the accused at the time of the organization of the court for his trial, as also at all the material stages and portions of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the accused escapes or departs, the record should state this at the first session where he is absent and note absence at each session if the court continues (compare Long v. State).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show convening order read to accused and opportunity to object
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should show that the order or orders convening the court and detailing the members were read to the accused or communicated to him, and that he was afforded an opportunity of objecting to any member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should clearly appear that the privilege of challenge (article 88) was extended; the precise phrasing of the question/answer need not be given, but the presence or content of objections should be recorded. If a specific challenge is offered, preferably record it in the accused's own terms, the remarks of the member, the action of the court, and any evidence introduced on the challenge (R. 2, 83; G. 16471).

rubrics_metrics.name: When new member joins, record opportunity to object
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a member is added at a subsequent stage of the proceedings, the record should show that the accused was afforded an opportunity of objecting to him and should set forth the action taken if objection was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R. 8, 662; include remarks and action on the objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court must extend right of challenge (obligation on court)
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of challenge guaranteed to the accused can be exercised by him only when the opportunity to do so is extended by the court; there is no obligation on the accused to demand his statutory rights — the obligation is on the court to see they are accorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record does not show affirmatively that the opportunity was accorded, no intendment of regularity can be made in favor of the record; the extension of the opportunity is vital and must be shown affirmatively (G. 18764; 28190).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show members and judge advocate were duly sworn
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should show that the members and the judge advocate were qualified by being duly sworn, and this should be shown in the record of every case tried by the same court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved form: 'The members of the court and the judge advocate were then duly sworn.' Where an absent member joins or a new judge advocate is detailed later, the record should show that such person was sworn before acting (R. 35, 8; R. 3, 548; C. 5323).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arraignment and pleas must be set forth
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should set forth the arraignment of the accused on the charges and specifications, with the plea or pleas made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If special pleas are interposed, the issue joined and action taken should be clearly stated. Charges and specifications should be embodied in the record instead of being merely referred to as annexed (R. 2, 83; R. 14, 39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record meetings with no business and state reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of a trial by court-martial should include a record of meetings where no business is transacted, together with a statement of the reason why none was transacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recess entries: if noted, show reassembly presence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not customary to take notice of a mere recess; but if a recess be noted at all, it should appear from the record that, on the reassembling, the members, judge advocate, and accused were duly present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages of proceedings must appear in proper order
rubrics_metrics.description: The several stages of the proceedings should appear in the record in the proper order (for example, swearing of the court should not be recorded before the statement about whether the accused objected to any members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening of each day's session may mention that previous proceedings were read and approved when that occurred; such reading is desirable but often not resorted to (R. 11, 1; R. 25, 349; 34, 167).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions must be recorded as new independent chapter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the court is reassembled for revision of its proceedings, the record should formally recite all that is ordered and done as a new and independent chapter of the history of the case, beginning with a copy of the order reconvening the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record should show at least five members assembled with judge advocate and, if proper, the accused; the action taken under the order and final authentication by signatures of president and judge advocate. Corrections should be declared made with reference to the part of the original proceedings; original error must be left as recorded — erasure/interlineation is irregular (R. 1, 487; R. 11, 93; P. 23, 345).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record should note judge advocate withdrawal on close
rubrics_metrics.description: When the court closes, the record should properly set forth that the judge advocate withdrew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act of July 27, 1892 noted this; absence of such a statement will not impair legal validity — if record simply shows the court 'closed' presumption is that legal requirements were observed (P. 56, 387; P. 65, 350).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record all testimony, oral as nearly in witness's words
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should fully set forth all the testimony introduced upon the trial — the oral portion as nearly as practicable in the precise words of the witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is a gross irregularity for a judge-advocate to record only testimony he considered material or to summarize testimony (R. 2, 23; R. 3, 189; R. 20, 42).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify who introduced witness and who questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: It is usual and proper (though not essential) to specify by which party the witness is introduced and by whom the questions are put, and to designate the point at which prosecution closed and defense testimony commenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record that witnesses were duly sworn
rubrics_metrics.description: It should appear that each witness was duly sworn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While it should appear each witness was sworn, it is not customary to add that he was sworn in the presence of the accused; that is presumed absent contrary statement (R. 3, 550; R. 21, 143; R. 34, 457; R. 9, 166).

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections to admissibility should be set forth with argument and ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections taken to the admissibility of testimony should be set forth with the argument had thereon, if any, and the ruling of the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the court is closed on any interlocutory objection, that fact should be noted (R. 26, 643; R. 9, 221).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record need not show offer of cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The record need not show affirmatively that the accused was offered an opportunity to cross-examine; if it appears he did not cross-examine the presumption is that he waived the privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, the record need not state that the accused was notified of his privilege of being assisted by counsel (P. 44, 456).

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony of accused when sworn to be recorded like other witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the accused desires to be sworn and testifies in his own defense, his testimony is recorded like that of any other witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each case record must be complete in itself
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of each case — where several cases are tried by the same court — should 'be complete in itself' and as much an entirety as if it were the only case tried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each record should be separate and distinct, prepared and transmitted as disconnected documents; where a sentence is pronounced, the record should contain everything necessary to sustain it in fact and in law (R. 3, 402; R. 32, 130).

rubrics_metrics.name: Death sentence must show two-thirds concurrence
rubrics_metrics.description: In a case of a death sentence the record should state that it was concurred in by two-thirds of the members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must set forth finding on each charge and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should set forth the finding on each of the several charges and specifications, and proper entry as to previous convictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate need not record advising accused of privilege to testify before assembling
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not essential that the record show that the judge advocate called the attention of the accused to the fact of his privilege of testifying in his own behalf; General Order 75 requires only that this be done 'before the assembling of the court.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: reviewing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing authority designates the officer whose province and duty it is to take action upon the proceedings of a court-martial after they are terminated and to approve or disapprove the sentence; ordinarily the commander who convened the court, or his successor in command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: XIV A1–A3: in absence or change of command, successor or 'officer commanding for the time being' exercises authority (B. 13, 468; C. 5151; C. 5231).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing officer acts judicially and ministerially and is final in his functions
rubrics_metrics.description: In acting upon proceedings the legal reviewing officer acts partly in a judicial and partly in a ministerial capacity; he 'decides' and 'orders,' and the due exercise of his proper functions cannot be revised by superior military authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reviewing officer who has acted and promulgated his action cannot be required by a higher commander to revoke such action; relief for unwarranted sentence is by pardon or remission; if void for want of jurisdiction it may be set aside (R. 49, 264; G. 11509; G. 17386).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander cannot delegate reviewing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A military commander cannot delegate to an inferior or other officer his function as reviewing authority, nor regularly authorize a staff or other officer to subscribe for him the action of approval/disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals or actions subscribed by staff officers purporting to be by the commander or 'in the absence and by the direction of' are irregular and open to question (R. 4, 567; R. 9, 27; R. 27, 297).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority's criticism not protected by official privilege in certain civil actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If criticism by the reviewing authority of an individual is made the subject of an action at law, the reviewer could not plead that his comment was protected by official privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 14002, July 9, 1903 — caution about civil liability for reviewer's comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority cannot approve sentence when reviewed accused is not in service
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier was dishonorably discharged and thereafter a record of another trial completed before his discharge was placed before the reviewing authority, the reviewing authority had no right to approve the second sentence because he was not then in the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 13926, Jan. 12, 1903; statutory exceptions concerning confinement after dishonorable discharge do not apply to offenses alleged to have been committed before discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquittal is a sentence and inchoate until reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquittal is a sentence in the sense of judgment and is ordinarily inchoate until acted on by the reviewing authority; it may be returned by the reviewing authority for reconsideration by the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing officer cannot correct record by striking out findings or substituting findings
rubrics_metrics.description: A reviewing officer cannot himself correct the record by striking out any part of the finding or sentence, or otherwise substitute a finding for that of the court; he may, however, specify reasons for his action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If he desires to amend the record he should reconvene the court for that purpose. Instances: approving only included offense of absence without leave was unauthorized; ordering words 'without criminality' treated as struck out was beyond authority (R. 47, 291; R. 12, 250).

rubrics_metrics.name: No military authority may add to punishment imposed by court
rubrics_metrics.description: No military authority, whether reviewing officer or other commander, can add to a punishment as imposed by a court-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cannot add forfeiture of pay, fine, corporal punishment, confinement, hard labor, or other penalties not adjudged by the sentence. Executive orders cannot lawfully prescribe punishments not adjudged (R. 2, 444; R. 20, 430; C. 8977). Specific examples show increasing weight for carrying, adding confinement when only forfeiture adjudged, imposing hard labor when sentence was confinement only, or ordering confinement to enforce a fine is illegal (R. 27, 511; R. 11, 98; R. 20, 340).

rubrics_metrics.name: Penitentiary confinement not legalized by labelling as 'military prison'
rubrics_metrics.description: Penitentiary confinement cannot be legalized as punishment for purely military offenses by designating a penitentiary as a 'military prison' and ordering confinement there of soldiers sentenced to imprisonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings need not be expressly approved after 1892 amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: It is no longer necessary that the findings of a court-martial should be expressly approved; the act of July 27, 1892 requires only that the sentence be approved by the reviewing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to cases requiring Presidential confirmation as well as others (C. 2844; C. 5095; C. 12723).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing officer should reconvene court to correct material errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reviewing officer deems the proceedings of the court materially erroneous or ill-advised, his proper course generally is to reconvene the court for the purpose of having the defect corrected, furnishing it with the grounds of his opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If he regards a sentence as inadequate he should state why when reassembling; though he cannot compel the court to adopt his views, he may express formal disapprobation of the court's refusal (R. 11, 440; R. 4, 579; C. 14260).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid general findings where specific offense proven
rubrics_metrics.description: A general finding such as 'conduct to the prejudice...' for a charge of 'conduct unbecoming' should not be resorted to where the specific offense charged is substantially made out by the testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If facts clearly establish a specific dishonorable behavior, a mere general finding should not be approved and the court should be reconvened to obtain a finding in accordance with the facts (R. 30, 495).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variance in date/place not fatal if not essential and act identified
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the offense is alleged to have been committed on a particular day but proof shows a different day, if time is not of the essence and the act is sufficiently identified by other testimony, the variance will not be a fatal defect and need not induce disapproval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A return of the record to the court for correction, if practicable, is advisable (R. 13, 361).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of regularity absent obvious irregularity
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a presumption, in the absence of obvious irregularity, that the proceedings were regular and according to law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss/destruction of record before review renders proceedings inoperative
rubrics_metrics.description: If the record of the trial is lost or destroyed before any action by the reviewing authority and the court cannot be reconvened to remake the record from original notes, the proceedings should be considered inoperative and the sentence of no effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies where complete destruction by fire or loss of stenographic notes makes intelligent review impossible (R. 6, 582; P. 55, 181; C. 24198).

rubrics_metrics.name: Misnaming or misdescription must be objected by plea in abatement
rubrics_metrics.description: A misnaming or misdescription of the rank of the accused in the specification should be taken advantage of by exception in the nature of a plea in abatement; where not objected to, the error is immaterial after sentence provided the accused is sufficiently identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical spelling errors (idem sonans) immaterial
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere clerical error in the spelling of the name of the accused, leaving it idem sonans, is not a case of misnomer and does not affect the validity of the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission/indefiniteness of time or place: amendment or immaterial if unobjected
rubrics_metrics.description: Where time or place is omitted or averred without sufficient definiteness and the defect is excepted to by the accused on pleading, the court will direct an amendment; but if no objection is interposed, proceedings will be sufficient if time/place can be made out with reasonable certainty from testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in citing old article numbers require abatement objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges laid under old article numbers (instead of new ones) are errors that can only be taken advantage of by an objection in the nature of a plea in abatement; in the absence of such objection the mistake is immaterial after finding and sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal hostility of judge advocate does not affect validity
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the judge advocate was personally objectionable or hostile to the accused could not affect the validity of the proceedings of a court-martial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of shackles or ball-and-chain during hearing does not invalidate proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that an accused soldier was tried with hands or feet in shackles, or with ball-and-chain attached, omitted to be removed during hearing, does not affect the legality of the proceedings or sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although reprehensible, such treatment does not invalidate proceedings (R. 50, 33; R. 63, 196; R. 55, 686).
